new_scholarship.description: The Mana Tūāpapa Future Leader Fellowship is the early-career scheme within the Aotearoa New Zealand Tāwhia te Mana Research Fellowships, administered by Royal Society Te Apārangi on behalf of the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment. It funds employed researchers within 0-4 years of research experience after PhD conferral to build the foundations of an independent research career. Around 20 fellowships are awarded each year, each worth NZ$820,000 over four years, made up of salary contribution, institutional overheads and research expenses. The scheme replaced the previous Rutherford Discovery, Rutherford Foundation and James Cook Research Fellowships.

new_scholarship.description: The Rhodes Scholarship for New Zealand is a partnership between the Rhodes Trust and the Robertson Foundation, administered in New Zealand by Universities New Zealand – Te Pōkai Tara. It supports outstanding all-round students to undertake postgraduate study at the University of Oxford, United Kingdom. Up to three scholars are elected from New Zealand each year, and the Scholarship covers fees, accommodation and living costs for up to three years. Applicants must be New Zealand citizens or hold a New Zealand Permanent Resident Visa and must meet an age and undergraduate GPA requirement.

They are awarded to exceptional Māori students for vocational or tertiary study who demonstrate values aligned with those of the 28th (Māori) Battalion. Following a $100,000 per year increase from the 2026-27 Budget, 14 scholarships are awarded each year across five schemes: 5 VET, 4 undergraduate, 3 master's, 1 Master of Education research and 1 doctoral. VET applicants need a certificate or diploma at NZQA levels 4 to 7 (minimum 120 credits, full time) and cannot be studying a bachelor's degree.

programme_detail_official.description: The University of Otago International Master's Research Scholarship provides funding to support international Master's students at the University of Otago. It pays a stipend of NZ$18,204 per annum plus a tuition fee waiver for one year capped at NZ$35,000 for Master's study, excluding the student services fee and insurance. Four awards are offered, normally one per Academic Division. Applicants must be international students obtaining their first Master's qualification and undertaking a thesis-based Master's; selection is based predominantly on academic merit and research potential.
